grade.label: fail
grade.reason: The agent planned to run a separate frontend dev server but never executed that step (and the repair agent fixed an unrelated import path instead of the missing built index.html), so the Flask health check kept hitting a template that was never generated.
grade.wentWrong: The plan called for two components — the Flask backend (`app.py serve`) and the React dev server (`npm start`) — run separately per the README, but the executed command trail only shows `npm install` and repeated `python app.py serve --port 8000` calls; no `npm start`/frontend launch ever ran, so the React build/dev index.html was never produced or served. Health checks then hit Flask's `/` route, which does `render_template("index.html")` and threw `jinja2.exceptions.TemplateNotFound: index.html` because Flask's template folder only gets populated by a built frontend. The repair agent misdiagnosed this: its one patch added a sys.path bootstrap to `app.py` for package imports, which has nothing to do with the missing template, so the same 500 recurred until the 45-minute timeout. For this to work, the agent needed to either actually start/build the React frontend as its own plan specified, or point the health check at the frontend dev server's port instead of Flask's.
